title: How OpenEvidence scales medical search for 650K doctors
description: OpenEvidence on Vercel Serves 650,000 doctors with medical search Completes production deployments in about five minutes Absorbs traffic spikes without additional capacity provisioning Reduced serverless spend by 90% with Fluid compute Updates doctor- and patient-facing applications independently OpenEvidence helps physicians find medical evidence during care, whether they’re checking a dosage on intensive care rounds or handling a case outside their specialty without a specialist nearby. Answers draw on peer-reviewed literature and include citations, so doctors can examine the sources behind them. OpenEvidence’s small team began using Vercel to get early experiments online and kept that workflow as the product grew, relying on the platform to handle web deployments and capacity. Building software physicians depend on The stakes are different when software helps inform medical decisions. An incorrect answer can affect how a doctor treats a patient, while an unavailable application can cut off access to evidence when it is needed. OpenEvidence supported more than 20 million clinical consultations in January 2026 . The company also reported that more than 100 million Americans were treated by doctors using OpenEvidence in 2025 . "Honestly, life or death is not inaccurate," says Kush Khosla, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. "We operate in situations where it's an ER and they really need to know what's going on. Uptime is very, very important to us." "A lot of doctors and medical professionals are used to really outdated software," says Andy Yoon, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. A more modern experience still needs to meet physicians' expectations of speed, stability, clarity, and information they can trust. The small team needs a way to test updates to the web application before putting them into production and to roll back if something goes wrong. Keeping releases simple as the audience grows Andy recalls why Vercel suited the team he joined at OpenEvidence. "I was pretty much the only engineer on our team coming from an actual frontend background," he says. "Most of our team works in Python and machine learning." He adds, "Given the makeup of our engineering team, Vercel really scaled with our needs so well." The team builds its physician-facing web application with the Next.js framework . When engineers push changes to a development branch, Vercel builds and deploys a preview , giving them a link they can use for live demos and share with colleagues to try new features. Pushing or merging into the production branch then triggers the production build and deployment. If a release needs reverting, the team can roll back to a previous deployment . That workflow lets the team release multiple times a day, with each change becoming available to a physician audience that Kush thinks about whenever he ships something: More doctors without more provisioning Keeping that application available means handling demand the team can’t always anticipate. Andy was scrolling through Slack when he saw the message that OpenEvidence had gone viral on TikTok, reaching around two million views in under a week. He watched traffic climb and checked the logs. Response times stayed fast and error rates remained near zero , and with no additional capacity to provision, he went back to his work. Beyond sudden spikes, the team has accommodated sustained growth without rebuilding the web application. "Not once have I had to think, now that we have five times as many doctors, what's happening to page loads or time to first paint," Kush says. "The scaling has happened so naturally that we end up focusing on other things." A 90% drop in serverless spend As usage grew, VP of Engineering Micah Smith was watching compute costs. The team enabled Fluid compute for its functions on Vercel, and Micah described the result alongside the wider infrastructure budget: "We reduced our serverless spend by 90% while maintaining the same performance, and even as we've scaled up to 1000x growth, Vercel is less than 5% of our overall infra spend." Fluid compute lets multiple requests share a running function instance, so it can handle other work while a request waits for another service, such as a database or an AI backend, to respond. With Active CPU pricing , that waiting time doesn’t incur CPU charges, though memory remains billed while requests are in progress. A familiar workflow for a new audience Take Home, OpenEvidence’s first patient-facing application, lets a doctor translate a clinical answer into plain language and share it with a patient, who logs in to review and save the evidence. Clinical-trial matching is also part of the application’s planned direction. To support this expansion, the team uses a pattern established through dozens of early proofs of concept, each deployed as its own Vercel project with a custom domain. Stakeholders could open those applications and test the workflows for themselves. Getting new projects online in minutes helped the team find product-market fit and made it easier to win early enterprise partnerships. Take Home has its own project and domain too, so engineers can update the patient experience without deploying the other applications. With Take Home, evidence that helps a doctor during a consultation can become something a patient returns to afterward. About OpenEvidence: OpenEvidence helps healthcare professionals find medical evidence at the point of care, with answers sourced, cited, and grounded in peer-reviewed literature. Physicians use it daily across more than 10,000 hospitals and medical centers in the United States. Its mission is to help doctors save lives and improve patient care. Learn more at openevidence.com . Read more

title: Tencent Hy4 now available on AI Gateway
description: Hy4 from Tencent is now available on AI Gateway , at 50% off through December 31, 2026. Hy4 supports reasoning , tool calling , structured outputs , and image input, and has a 1M-token context window for work across a codebase or many documents. Hy4 is the first Hy model with vision. It can pick out fine detail in an image and read complex charts. It also supports computer use in both command-line and graphical interfaces. Compared with Hy4 Preview , it follows instructions more closely and does better with long context, long-running tasks, and deep research. Use tencent/hy4 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select tencent/hy4 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Hy4 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. title: Diagnose Vercel CLI setup problems with vercel doctor
description: Vercel CLI now includes vercel doctor , which checks your setup and shows the command that fixes each problem it finds. It checks the CLI version and install, your login and current team, the project link, and your project configuration in vercel.json . It also reports active incidents from the Vercel status page. Each check reports OK, Warning, Failed, or Skipped. When vercel upgrade can't update the installed CLI, the install check shows where the CLI runs from and how to reinstall it. Doctor runs without a login or a linked project, and it never prompts, logs in, or links a project, so coding agents can run it before guessing at a fix. Add --json to get each check's status and suggested commands as structured output. Update to the latest CLI version and run vercel doctor to check your setup, or read the doctor command reference. title: Introducing Vercel Security Review
description: Today, we are launching Vercel Security Review in public beta. Security Review is a new capability in Vercel Agent , alongside Code Review and Investigation. Once enabled, it scans for vulnerabilities on every push to a team's connected GitHub repositories. Findings appear as comments on pull requests, are listed in the Security dashboard, and are available via CLI. With your permission, Vercel Agent can also validate and push fixes for findings. How it works Security reviews are triggered by GitHub push events, including direct pushes to your production branch. In monorepos, reviews are scoped to the project's root directory. Here is how it works: You push code to a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project. As soon as the push lands, Security Review scans the changed code for vulnerabilities like missing authorization checks or exposed secrets. Findings are posted to the Security dashboard. On private and internal repositories, Security Review also adds a GitHub check to the commit and comments on the pull request. You can fix findings by clicking Fix with Vercel Agent in the dashboard, or use the CLI to pull findings and have your own coding agent implement changes. When subsequent security reviews no longer detect a finding, it is marked as no longer detected in the dashboard, and the GitHub comment is closed. Each review compares the push against a base and covers only what changed. For deployments, the base is the branch’s previous deployment, so the agent reviews the change against what’s already running. Because it only scans the diff, Security Review finishes in seconds and can run on every preview and production deployment. What the agent checks The agent reads the diff along with the surrounding code, traces how the changed code can be reached, checks for existing protections, and rechecks each finding before reporting it. That process is how it catches logic flaws like missing authorization checks, which pattern-matching scanners miss. Each review also applies your team’s security policies , which you can write in plain language and apply to specific projects or across your team. For example, a policy can require any endpoint that returns customer data to check that the requester owns it. You can also manage policies with the Vercel CLI, using vercel security policy . How findings are tracked Each new finding is checked against ones that have already been reported, so the same issue isn’t flagged twice. Every finding is tied to the deployment where it first appeared and changes are followed from there. That means that when a vulnerable change from a pull request is merged into your production branch, the finding is flagged in production as well. When a later review no longer detects the issue in an environment, the agent marks the finding as no longer detected there. Acting on findings Every finding explains the vulnerability and how to fix it, with links to the commit and deployment where it first appeared. Findings are listed in the Vulnerability view in the Security dashboard, where you can ask Vercel Agent to validate and commit fixes. Findings are also available via CLI , so you can fix vulnerabilities with your own coding agent. Each new finding generates an audit log event, which Enterprise teams can send to their SIEM through Audit Log Drains . Here is a demo of sample findings in the dashboard: Fixing vulnerabilities with Vercel Agent When Vercel Agent can fix a finding, you will see the option to click Fix with Vercel Agent on the finding page in the dashboard. After you click, the agent confirms the vulnerability still exists, then makes the smallest change that fixes it and updates the tests. Say a developer pushes a change to an invoice download endpoint, and the lookup doesn't check which organization the invoice belongs to. Within seconds, Security Review flags that any signed-in user could download another organization's invoice by changing its ID. Vercel Agent's fix scopes the lookup to the user's organization: Fixing vulnerabilities with your own coding agent You can point your coding agent or other systems at the Vercel CLI to pull and fix vulnerabilities: Findings in the dashboard also give you the ability to copy details as Markdown or JSON , making it easy to paste them into an agent conversation. Every code change needs security review Frontier AI models are making vulnerabilities far easier to find and exploit. Last month, researchers turned two decade-old flaws in PHP core into working remote code execution exploits with relatively little effort. At the same time, agents are writing more of the code teams ship, and each handles security review its own way, or in many cases, not at all. With Vercel Security Review, you can scan every push on every project for vulnerabilities by default, using the security policies you set. What's next Security Review starts with code pushed to GitHub. Next, we're bringing it to deployments from the Vercel CLI and v0, and to repositories that don't deploy on Vercel. We're also working on suggested fixes you can apply directly from the pull request. Get started Vercel Security Review is available today in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. To get started, enable Security Review in Vercel Agent Settings . You can choose to run Security Review on all projects, or only the ones you choose. To learn more, read the Changelog entry and the Security Review documentation . Security Review is billed at the Vercel Agent rate , with model tokens at the provider's rate and no markup, plus $0.25 per million tokens. Security reviews are free until November 10, 2026. Fixes made with Vercel Agent are billed at the rate above. Read more
